classification.difficultyReason: Model the foam as an outer solid minus an inner cavity, then distinguish the three exposed surfaces when a can covers the interior.

content.prompt: A foam drink-can holder is in the shape of a cylinder. The inside radius is 5.5 cm and the inside height is 11 cm. The foam is 1 cm thick and forms the curved surface of the cylinder. The base is cut out of foam 1 cm thick. Give exact answers and approximations correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source schematic open cylindrical foam holder: outer radius6.5, inner5.5, outer height12, inner11, closed base1. No numeric dimensions added. Exact coaxial top ellipses, outer tangent generators and near/far bottom rim; dashed inner generators/floor are source explanatory concealed interior construction, not visible outside seams.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens, no computed answer values.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the volume inside the cylinder in cubic centimetres.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the volume of foam in the drink-can holder in cubic centimetres.

answer.worked:
The outer radius is 6.5 cm and the outside height is 12 cm, including the 1 cm base. Subtract the empty interior.
$$\begin{aligned}V_{\text{foam}}&=\pi(6.5)^2(12)-332.75\pi\\V_{\text{foam}}&=174.25\pi\text{ cm}^3\approx547.42\text{ cm}^3.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If a cylindrical drink can perfectly fills the holder, find the total surface area of the exposed foam in square centimetres.

answer.worked:
The can covers the inner wall and inner floor. Exposed foam is the outside curved wall, outside bottom and top annulus.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2\pi(6.5)(12)+\pi(6.5)^2+\pi(6.5^2-5.5^2)\\S&=(156+42.25+12)\pi\\S&=210.25\pi\text{ cm}^2\approx660.52\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
